   "source": [
    "# Tools for Generating Cell Placements\n",
    "\n",
    "BMTK provides several tools to facilitate cell placement, although users are always welcome to place their neuronal somata according to their own custom generated positions. We provide functions for simple geometries and placement based on geometries or densities from \\*.nrrd files. Units can be placed with a minimum distance between them (please see second part of this tutorial)."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "9cdb59ae",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Generate a cylindrical column of cell positions\n",
    "\n",
    "This function places random locations uniformly within a cylinder or cylindrical ring. Note that 'y' is the vertical axis."

    "## Generate random locations according to an NRRD file \n",
    "\n",
    "We may want to place the units according to a file containing 3D location information, such as the [Allen Brain Atlas Common Coordinate Framework](https://help.brain-map.org/display/mouseconnectivity/API#API-DownloadAtlas3-DReferenceModels). You can obtain a structural mask that describes the extent of a structure of interest. Cells will be placed randomly within that structure at a density of max_dens. If the \\*.nrrd file contains varying cell densities, this function can also be used to place cells randomly according to that density raster.\n",
    "\n",
    "You will need to install the ```pynrrd``` library to use this function.\n",
    "\n",
    "Note that the units of cell density are in cells/mm<sup>3</sup> while positions are in units of microns.\n",
    "\n",
    "If the structure is bilateral and only one half is desired for modeling, you can specify the axis along which to split it."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 5,
   "id": "0629af55",

   "source": [
    "## Cell placements with minimum distance between units\n",
    "\n",
    "The same built-in placement options above are available now with a minimum distance enforced between cells. With the use of the cell placement object, multiple populations can be placed at the same time, but must use the same minimum distance, which is enforced between and within populations.\n",
    "\n",
    "For a given minimum distance, there is a maximum density above which it will be physically impossible to pack the units. The functions will inform users of the packing limit for random close packing or hexagonal close packing. The default method is progressive sampling ('prog'), which iteratively replaces units that violate the minimum distance until the final density is achieved. As this can be slow to run when the requested density is near the packing limit, you may set `verbose` to True to monitor the progress. You may find that in such cases just slightly decreasing the dmin value significantly speeds up the run.\n",
    "\n",
    "The alternative jittered lattice method ('lattice') may be faster at very high density and may allow you to slightly exceed the random close packing limit, but produces an unrealistic geometric regularity in order to achieve those densities.  "
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",

   "source": [
    "from bmtk.builder.auxi.node_params import CellLocations\n",
    "\n",
    "filename = './sources/nrrd/structure_721.nrrd'\n",
    "\n",
    "max_dens = 100000\n",
    "\n",
    "ctx = CellLocations('cortex')\n",
    "ctx.dmin = 18.0\n",
    "ctx.CCF_orientation=True   # Use Allen Common Coordinate Framework orientation with y-axis as vertical\n",
    "\n",
    "ctx.add_positions_nrrd(filename, max_dens, pop_names=['Pyr'], split_bilateral='z', method='prog', verbose=True)\n",
    "\n",
    "ctx.plot_locs()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "bc0c95d9",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "It is preferable to use partitioning (with the `pop_names` and `partitions` keywords) to place units by the same general rule into the same spatial structure. In the example below, the first call to `add_positions_nrrd()` assigns 85% of returned cells to Pyr and 15% to PV. However, you can also add placements iteratively (second call to `add_positions_nrrd()`)."
   ]
  },

   "source": [
    "Once we are satisfied with the placement, we can pass them to `add_nodes()` as follows (based on the ellipsoid example directly above):"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 13,
   "id": "13e4cf10",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "from bmtk.builder.networks import NetworkBuilder\n",
    "\n",
    "net = NetworkBuilder('cortex')\n",
    "net.add_nodes(N=ctx.Pyr.N,\n",
    "              positions=ctx.Pyr.positions,\n",
    "              pop_name='Pyr', location='VisL4', ei='e',  # optional parameters\n",
    "              model_type='point_process',  # Tells the simulator to use point-based neurons\n",
    "              model_template='nest:iaf_psc_alpha',  # tells the simulator to use NEST iaf_psc_alpha models\n",
    "              dynamics_params='472363762_point.json'  # File containing iaf_psc_alpha model parameters\n",
    "             )\n",
    "\n",
    "net.add_nodes(N=ctx.PV.N,\n",
    "              positions=ctx.PV.positions,\n",
    "              pop_name='PV', location='VisL4', ei='i',  # optional parameters\n",
    "              model_type='point_process',  # Tells the simulator to use point-based neurons\n",
    "              model_template='nest:iaf_psc_alpha',  # tells the simulator to use NEST iaf_psc_alpha models\n",
    "              dynamics_params='472912177_point.json'  # File containing iaf_psc_alpha model parameters\n",
    "             )"
   ]
